newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan shipping shares up on easing China ties.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan shipping shares up on easing China ties.

text.p: Taiwan's shipping shares were higher at mid-morning on Tuesday, reflecting expectations of easing relations between Taiwan and China, brokers said.
After 90 minutes, Yang Ming Marine jumped T$1.4 or 4.23 percent to T$34.5 and Wan Hai Lines rose T$2.0 or 2.65 percent to T$77.5.

"Shipping shares are usually very sensitive about any signs of easing tensions across the Taiwan strait. Some people believe the government will offer new olive branch to thaw the frozen ties," said Lin Long-hsien, an analyst of United Securities.
Local shipping firms have pressured the government to allow direct sea links between Taiwan and mainland China to save transportation costs.
On Monday, Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party completed the draft of a treaty for peace with China, proposing talks to end an icy 17-month impasse with its longtime rival.
President Lee Teng-hui's renewed invitation on Sunday to China's leaders to visit Taiwan was also taken as a positive sign, Lin said.

A political impasse between Taiwan and China, rivals since a civil war ended in 1949, started in June 1995 after President Lee made a private visit to the United States, which Beijing saw as a move to promote independence.
